reason: I want to see what happens to the orange star as the galaxies pass through each other.
expectation: The stars may pass into the other galaxy's outskirts without colliding, though their paths could change.

alternatives.reason: The crossing gas addresses the other goal, but I want to follow the orange light first.

effect: The orange star survives in a stream, completing that goal; I'll follow the gas next.
reaction: The contrast between disrupted galactic shape and surviving stars is striking.
reason: The dense gas crossing seems a direct way to investigate where the gas goes.
expectation: The gas streams may collide and compress, though I'm unsure what structure will result.

alternatives.reason: The thin gas could also reveal what happens in the crossing, but the dense lane seems more central.

effect: The dense gas collides, heats and cools into a denser gathering, unlike the passing stars; the gas goal remains open.
reaction: The contrast with the stars is satisfying, especially that only some gas will form stars.
reason: I'll follow the thin gas next to see whether it behaves differently at the crossing.
expectation: I expect the thin gas to interact with the crossing gas, but I'm unsure whether it will gather or disperse.

alternatives.reason: The distant cloud may show where gas ends up, but I want to finish exploring the crossing first.

effect: The thin gas forms a hot, diffuse bridge rather than promptly collapsing into stars; the gas goal remains open.
reaction: The different outcomes for dense and thin gas make the crossing more interesting.
reason: The cloud at the outskirts is the only remaining offered action, and may show where gas goes next.
expectation: The cloud may encounter gas in the other galaxy's outskirts, though I don't know what will result.

effect: The outer cloud misses the collision and is pulled outward with the stars, completing the gas goal and the chapter.
reaction: The distinction between tidal stretching and a direct collision was interesting.

mostWorthwhile.text: The dense-gas collision was most worthwhile: it contrasted with the stars passing between one another and explained how gas heats, cools and gathers.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final cloud action was less engaging as a decision because it was the only offered action, though its result was informative.

surprise.text: The outer cloud could be drawn out with the stars without entering the main gas collision.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although the compatible-options menu supplied the pairings rather than requiring me to discover them.

continue.text: Yes. The contrasting paths of stars and gas made me curious about what the displaced material encounters next.
